body:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 4567 - RESOLVED
Summary: We saw elevated 5xx and timeouts from the embeddings endpoint between ~02:32-03:05 UTC. Initial mitigation: rolled back release 2026.11.03-embed, scaled up Dedicated pool capacity for embeddings, and cleared KV cache entries. Post-rollback metrics look stable.

Maya Patel: Thanks all — great quick work. I'll schedule a 30m postmortem. Proposed: tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Can someone own the RCA?

Tom O'Connor: I can own timeline collection and evidence (logs/traces). I'll start pulling traces and machine metrics now.

Priya Shah: I can dig into the batching/kv cache change that shipped in 2026.11.03-embed. From a quick glance the continuous-batching change may have allowed oversized batches with quantized models, causing memory pressure. I'll open an investigation PR and aim for a fix + tests.

Carlos Nguyen: Support here — I've started a customer-impact list (internal). We have ~14 customers with elevated error rates, 3 with SLA-level impact. Draft of customer-facing note below — please review: 

Carlos Nguyen: > Hi there, we experienced a temporary degradation in embeddings that affected throughput and caused errors for some customers between 02:32-03:05 UTC. We rolled back a recent change and service is now stable. We're investigating root cause and will share an RCA in the next 72 hours. If you were impacted and need immediate help, reply and we'll prioritize.

Daniel Reiss: For status page, keep it concise. Proposed public status blurb:
```
Status: Degraded performance — RESOLVED
Impact: Reduced embedding throughput and increased errors for some customers (02:32-03:05 UTC)
Cause: Regression in batching logic causing memory pressure; rollback performed
Next steps: Postmortem scheduled; detailed RCA to follow within 72 hours
```

Evelyn Park: From customer success POV we should offer remediation credits for customers who hit SLA thresholds. I'll evaluate exposure and propose credit amounts within 24h. Recommend we not promise credits until we confirm scope.

Maya Patel: Action items so we don't lose track:
- timeline doc (owner: Tom O'Connor) — collect logs/traces and annotate (ETA: 24h)
- root cause analysis (owners: Priya Shah + Tom) — deep dive & hypothesis validation (ETA: 72h)
- fix + tests + canary (owner: Priya) — PR and small canary rollout to Dedicated pool (ETA: 72h)
- runbook/update (owner: Maya) — add prevention steps & paging tweaks (ETA: 5 days)
- customer comms draft + send (owners: Carlos Nguyen + Daniel Reiss) — send initial note tomorrow EOD, follow-up RCA link when ready
- billing/credits proposal (owner: Evelyn Park) — decision and amounts (ETA: 24h)

Tom O'Connor: I'll upload the timeline doc to the incidents folder and share link in the postmortem doc. Will include per-host OOM logs, kernel OOM, and batch-size histograms.

Priya Shah: I'll open a PR for a conservative batching cap and add unit tests to simulate quantized model memory usage. Tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-sre for review.

Carlos Nguyen: I'll prepare the status page draft and the customer email now and leave placeholders for the RCA link. Will not send until we agree wording.

Maya Patel: I'll create the postmortem doc and invite the participants above. Please add notes directly to the doc. Link: <internal:/incidents/postmortems/4567>

incident-bot: Reminder set — postmortem meeting in 24 hours (1977864177).

Maya Patel: For public messaging let's be conservative: acknowledge impact, confirm rollback and stability, and promise a full RCA in 72 hours. Avoid technical minutiae in the first message. :white_check_mark:

Evelyn Park: I'll prepare a short CS playbook for any customers who reply and escalate.

Daniel Reiss: Once Priya confirms the root cause language, I'll publish the status page update and coordinate the customer email send with Carlos.

Carlos Nguyen: Noted — I'll queue the email for manual send tomorrow and make sure Support is ready to triage replies.

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Let's make sure owners update the postmortem doc as work progresses. We'll review action item completion in 7 days and close the incident when all remediation and comms are done.
